subject: Concurrency / cost / latency tradeoff workbook — test plan and evidence request
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@cloudridge.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@procurecloud.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Reducing tail latency under concurrency — can Redwood run a custom matrix?

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the brief at last week's demo. As part of our RFP evaluation we need a tighter understanding of how latency and unit cost evolve under different concurrency and batch-size tradeoffs for a 13B conversational model. Specifically, procurement is asking for: 

1) A provided workbook showing tail (p95/p99) latency and tokens/sec across QPS targets: 10, 50, 200, 800.
2) Cost per 1M tokens for each operating point (including batching and quantization assumptions).
3) Test methodology: workload shape (prompt length dist, response length dist), KV/prefix cache behavior, warm/cold replica assumptions, and whether requests were routed to fallback variants.
4) Raw run artifacts and config so we can reproduce locally.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can run these custom experiments (or provide the workbook + raw traces) within the next 6 business days? We prefer an evidence-backed workbook rather than high-level numbers.

Best,
Maya
Head of Platform Procurement
CloudRidge

P.S. Procurement copied Tom from our SRE team who'll validate methodology.
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Reducing tail latency under concurrency — can Redwood run a custom matrix?

Team — forwarding CloudRidge's ask. High priority RFP; they want evidence and reproducibility. Preliminary answers below; will need Grace to own the run and Steph to produce the workbook and cost calc.

Quick plan:
- Grace: spin the capture using our internal harness (use test-harness-config.yml variant A: mix 60/40 prompt/response length, KV enabled). Run for targets: 10, 50, 200, 800 QPS. Capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cpu/gpu utilization, and tail latency distribution.
- Steph: compile workbook with sheets: run-summary, cost-breakdown, methodology, raw-run-links. Include assumptions (model: redwood-13b-v1, quant: 8-bit nf4 equivalent, batching policy: adaptive with max batch 32, prefix cache TTL: 5m).
- I will review and draft the external narrative/cover note.

Timebox: run by Tue EOD (2026-09-01), workbook to Maya by Wed morning. Any blockers shout now.

—Vivek
VP, Product & GTM
Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Reducing tail latency under concurrency — can Redwood run a custom matrix?

Vivek / Steph,

Acknowledged. Started a dry-run overnight on the staging pool (G5x2-equivalent nodes). Notes from the first pass:
- Workload shape used: prompt length distribution = {short: 35%, medium: 45%, long: 20%} where short ~ 12 tokens, medium ~ 64 tokens, long ~ 280 tokens. Response length target ~ 48 tokens median. (Attached config: test-harness-config.yml)
- Cache: prefix/KV caching enabled with 5m TTL and cold start every 10th request to simulate real-user variance.
- Batching: adaptive batching with latency SLO 80ms target at p50 for small prompts; for larger prompts throttle batching window to avoid memory pressure.

Preliminary single-run observation (200 QPS target, 8-bit quant): p50=18ms, p95=62ms, p99=110ms, tokens/sec=~42k, avg GPU util=64%. The p99 tail correlates strongly with long prompt mix and cold caches.

I'll run the four QPS targets now (10 / 50 / 200 / 800) with three repeats each and store compressed traces (raw-aggregate-runs-2026-08.zip). ETA end of day Tue.

Grace
Senior Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: test-harness-config.yml (text)]
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@cloudridge.com>, Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@procurecloud.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2026 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood workbook and evidence for concurrency/cost matrix — CloudRidge RFP (CR-2026-0920)

Hi Maya / Tom,

Thanks again for the ask — attached is the workbook and supporting artifacts from our runs. Short summary is below; the workbook contains per-run sheets and a methodology tab with exact config. Attachments: redwood-concurrency-workbook-v1.xlsx, raw-aggregate-runs-2026-08.zip.

Executive summary (see sheet 'run-summary'):
- Model: redwood-13b-v1 (8-bit quantized profile: q8nf4).
- QPS points tested: 10, 50, 200, 800. Each point: 3 independent 30-minute runs; reported numbers are median of runs.
- Key results (tokens per 1M and tail latency):
  * 10 QPS — p50 12ms / p95 34ms / p99 58ms — cost per 1M tokens: $5.80
  * 50 QPS — p50 16ms / p95 48ms / p99 94ms — cost per 1M tokens: $4.20
  * 200 QPS — p50 18ms / p95 62ms / p99 110ms — cost per 1M tokens: $3.10
  * 800 QPS — p50 29ms / p95 130ms / p99 290ms — cost per 1M tokens: $2.75 (note: at this point requests hit burst autoscale and fallback lanes intermittently)

Methodology highlights (also in workbook):
- Prompt/response length distributions as used in test-harness-config.yml.
- Warm/cold mix: 90% warm (cache hit) / 10% cold per run iteration.
- Fallback behavior: for 800 QPS runs we allowed fallback to a 7B-compatible variant when queueing exceeded 250ms; fallback rate is listed in the workbook.
- Cost calc: includes GPU-time + amortized instance overhead + networking; quantization overheads and batching efficiency are listed per sheet.

Actionable takeaway: for predictable p99 under 100ms at 200 QPS we recommend enabling prefix cache (>5m TTL) and a conservative adaptive-batch max of 24; this keeps fallback below 1.5% while preserving unit cost.

Files attached. Let us know if you'd like us to run a custom prompt-set (you can upload a representative corpus) or reproduce in your environment with our test harness.

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-concurrency-workbook-v1.xlsx (xlsx)]
[Attachment: raw-aggregate-runs-2026-08.zip (zip)]

Stephanie / team,

Thanks — workbook received and looks thorough. A couple quick clarifications before procurement sign-off: 

1) For the 800 QPS point you mention fallback to a 7B variant — can you quantify the quality delta (e.g., embedding/text-sim delta or sampling divergence) we should expect when fallback happens? Procurement wants an explicit note for SLA language.
2) Can you provide the exact command line and Docker image tag used for the harness runs so our SRE can sanity-check in a fenced environment?

If you can respond with a short addendum to the workbook (or a new sheet) we'll be able to move to commercial terms next week.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

—Tom
Senior SRE, CloudRidge
